title: Alphabet Inc. — Annual Report (SYNTHETIC FIXTURE for offline demo/evals)
body:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — This document is an invented excerpt in the style of a 10-K, bundled for offline demos and evaluation. Its figures are fictional and must not be used as financial data.

ITEM 1. BUSINESS

Alphabet Inc. is a collection of businesses, the largest of which is Google. Revenues for 2025 were $350.0 billion, an increase of 13 percent. Google Search and other revenues were $198.0 billion. YouTube advertising revenues were $36.1 billion. Google Cloud revenues were $43.2 billion, an increase of 31 percent year over year, with growing contribution from generative AI infrastructure and the Gemini family of models offered through Vertex AI. The Company's Gemini models are integrated across Search (AI Overviews), Workspace, Android and Cloud.

ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS

The Company faces significant legal and regulatory risk. In United States v. Google, the district court found that the Company maintained an illegal monopoly in general search, and remedy proceedings could result in restrictions on the Company's search distribution agreements, including payments to device manufacturers and browser developers for default placement (traffic acquisition costs were $54.3 billion in 2025). Adverse remedies could materially affect revenues. The shift of user behaviour toward AI chat experiences could reduce traditional search query volume, and monetisation of AI experiences is at an early stage. The Company also faces risks from the substantial capital expenditure — $75 billion planned for 2026 — required to build AI computing infrastructure.

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

Operating income for 2025 was $121.4 billion and operating margin was 35 percent. Other Bets losses were $4.1 billion. The Company repurchased $62.0 billion of its Class A and Class C shares and paid $9.8 billion in dividends during 2025, its second year of paying a quarterly dividend.
